description: Composite and fictional characters created to dramatize the Punjab narco-jihad subplot in Dhurandhar 2. These figures represent social and operational archetypes in the Indian Punjab drug-terror network rather than specific documented individuals.

characters.name: Gurbaaz Singh 'Pinda'
characters.archetype: Local Punjab drug distributor — mid-level node between cross-border suppliers and street dealers
characters.narrative_function: Humanizes the demand side of narco-jihad; shows how Afghan heroin corrupts ordinary Punjab youth into terror support infrastructure

characters.name: Prabhneet Singh
characters.archetype: Punjab police officer / intelligence source — caught between duty and community
characters.narrative_function: Represents Indian state's ground-level counter-narcotics challenge; potential asset or liability

characters.name: Veena
characters.archetype: Family member affected by drug network — victim perspective
characters.narrative_function: Emotional stakes; demonstrates societal damage motivating counter-operations

characters.name: Balwinder Sandhu
characters.archetype: Former athlete/military figure fallen into drug trade — 'wasted potential' symbol
characters.narrative_function: Represents how narco-jihad specifically targets disciplined/authoritative figures for corruption or elimination

characters.name: Balwant
characters.archetype: Enforcer/protection for drug network — street-level muscle
characters.narrative_function: Operational threat to Indian protagonists; disposable opposition

characters.name: MLA Sukhwinder
characters.archetype: Political patronage for drug network — corrupt elected official
characters.narrative_function: Shows political protection layer; explains why police operations face systemic obstacles

characters.name: Faizal
characters.archetype: Cross-border courier/ facilitator — Pakistani side logistics
characters.narrative_function: Operational connector; demonstrates network span from Karachi to Amritsar

characters.name: Uzair's Wife
characters.archetype: Family leverage point — humanizes Uzair Baloch beyond criminal network
characters.narrative_function: Adds personal dimension to adversary; potential leverage or vulnerability

real_world_anchor.historical_basis: Punjab opioid crisis (2010s-present), systematic ISI narco-terror operations, documented Khalistani-Pakistani ISI coordination
real_world_anchor.verification_status: REPRESENTATIVE — Individual figures fictional but social/operational patterns fully documented

oracle_note: These characters are NOT playable as query subjects (side≠'indian' for most, or fictional composites). They may appear as intelligence targets, network nodes, or adversary model references only.
